summary: Keep one canonical Modern Aviation platform. Correct the supportable Apollo and Tiger ownership chain and the March 2024 closing treatment, but preserve a freshly evidenced exact exception for Swiss Life Asset Managers because no direct source identifies whether its 2019 interest was sold, rolled, retained, distributed, or otherwise disposed of at the Apollo-led closing.
resolvedFormerBlockers: The direct CCPC determination establishes AP Novus Holding, L.P. and TIP MA Investments LP investing into Novus Holdings Parent, L.P., which indirectly holds all Modern Aviation equity under Apollo/Tiger joint control.

Tiger's manager-authored 2024 release and public retrospective establish that Fund II and its co-investors fully exited in March 2024 and that Tiger's third flagship fund and co-investors reinvested alongside Apollo.
Direct SEC filings establish Apollo Infrastructure Company and an AIOF III Novus co-invest vehicle, so a sole Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund III attribution is too narrow.

The Swiss Life manager-authored 2019 article establishes the historical 33% entry, and Tiger's 2026 Form ADV establishes continued non-zero gross assets in the named Swiss Life vehicle and feeders without supplying a holdings schedule.
